purpose: Buyer perspective and difficulty comparison; development only; never training data.

cases.title: Busy executive, not a high-difficulty sales examiner

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context
accountContext.notes: Development-only fixture, never added to the account library.

entries.text: The executive is between meetings with little attention, knows high-level complaints but not integrations, and has not invited a product presentation.
The executive personally wants to get to the next meeting; the seller's training success is irrelevant.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: I have a moment, then I need to go.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Omri from Salesforce. I wondered whether order-related service work is something your team wants to improve.

cases.manual_review: Look for ordinary brief engagement or low interest rather than a sophisticated sequence of proof requests. High difficulty must not increase technical knowledge or turn time pressure into a paragraph of useful discovery. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

cases.title: Real problem, root cause unknown

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context

entries.text: The executive has heard repeated complaints about long delivery investigations and cares about guest frustration.
The executive has not traced the process and does not know which system, team or handoff causes the delay. No exact impact baseline is available.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Those delivery calls do seem to take longer than they should.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: What is making them take so long?

cases.manual_review: Can the buyer care about a problem without diagnosing it? Missing root-cause knowledge should remain missing rather than becoming integration expertise or an ideal review agenda. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

cases.title: Knows the cause, does not prioritize fixing it

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context
accountContext.notes: Development-only fixture, never added to the account library.

entries.text: The manager knows a manual carrier-portal lookup is needed for occasional exceptional shipments.
The lookup is infrequent, has an accepted workaround and is not currently a meaningful priority. This lack of priority is established at all difficulty levels.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: For those unusual shipments, we look in the carrier portal.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: That sounds like something worth fixing. Would it help if it were all in one place?

cases.manual_review: Knowledge of a workflow must not become willingness to buy. Easy can be polite and cooperative without inventing urgency; Hard need not ask an elegant ROI challenge. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

cases.title: Buyer concern is their own workload

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context
accountContext.notes: Development-only fixture, never added to the account library.

entries.text: The director has capacity constraints because managers are supporting a seasonal staffing ramp.
The proposed review is vaguely described and the director does not know what work their team would have to do. They want to avoid a time-consuming project.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: We could do a workflow review with your team.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We are pretty stretched right now.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: It would help us understand the situation.

cases.manual_review: Does the reply come from capacity and effort on the buyer's side? A practical concern is appropriate; an invitation to deliver the perfect value proposition is not required. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

entries.text: The manager directly handles delivery exceptions but does not maintain a case-volume report.
The manager has limited attention during this exchange and has not investigated financial consequences.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: What do agents check, how often does that happen, and what does it cost you?

cases.manual_review: An incomplete answer is valid. Does the buyer avoid conveniently filling workflow, frequency and financial impact together? Do not impose a universal brevity rule. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

entries.text: The supervisor knows day-to-day case handling and has no access to budget decisions or procurement plans.
The supervisor does not know whether spending for this type of work has been approved and has no ready referral arranged.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Is there budget allocated to improve this?

cases.manual_review: Does the buyer admit the actual knowledge gap without inventing a number, volunteering an ideal sponsor, or constructing a qualification workaround? Difficulty must not supply missing knowledge. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. entries.text: The VP knows the service-operations lead owns the daily workflow, but has not decided that this conversation is useful.
The VP has not offered an introduction, a meeting or their own attendance. The issue is only a loosely described annoyance.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Someone in ops would know the details better than I do.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Understood. I do not yet know whether this matters enough to look at.

cases.manual_review: The buyer need not reward restraint with the ideal stakeholder and next-step plan. Referral can occur only if their actual motivation supports it, not because the seller needs progression. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

entries.text: The buyer is mildly curious but has not identified a priority, buying criteria or a specific question they need answered.
They are unsure whether this is worth attention and would not naturally know exactly what evidence would justify a meeting.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: I can send a short note about the idea.

cases.manual_review: Can the buyer leave the request simple rather than specifying the ideal metrics, attendees, technical proof and route to a meeting? Do not invent exact persuasion conditions. cases.title: Counterexample: motivated technical scrutiny

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context
accountContext.notes: Development-only fixture, never added to the account library.

entries.text: The director personally owns identity and access architecture and understands permission boundaries.
Their specific concern is preserving record-level access for third-party lookups. They genuinely need to understand whether the proposal respects that boundary.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Our agents do not all have access to the same records.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: The new workflow would make the order information available to agents.

cases.manual_review: A sharp permissions question is natural here. Anti-coach guidance must not suppress real expertise or make an engaged technical buyer evasive merely because difficulty is high. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.

cases.title: Counterexample: genuine interest and agreed follow-up

payload.context: Fictional buyer-only evaluation. Same known facts and transcript at each level; vary only unspecified commercial conditions.

accountContext.relationship: Existing Salesforce customer within this fictional exercise
accountContext.products: Service Cloud in this fictional exercise
accountContext.objective: Seller goal is intentionally excluded from buyer context
accountContext.notes: Development-only fixture, never added to the account library.

entries.text: The director has personally described a consequential workflow problem and explicitly agreed to a narrow follow-up with their team.
The purpose, attendees and time window were settled in the conversation; no new issue has emerged.

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: That review would be useful. Send the invite for Tuesday and I will bring our operations lead.

turns.speaker: seller
turns.text: Great. I will send the invite and a short outline today.

cases.manual_review: Preserve the actual agreement and allow a natural close at every level. Hard must not invent new resistance, and helpful cooperation is not automatically coach leakage when motivated by a real need. Compare levels 1, 3 and 5: commercial willingness/attention/disclosure may differ; knowledge and factual constraints must not. Do not grade by matching any exact phrase.
